executive_summary.company_overview: Thermify is a Welsh-headquartered seed-stage climate deeptech company developing HeatHub, a distributed micro data centre unit installed in homes that processes cloud computing workloads and captures waste heat to replace gas boilers for space heating and hot water. The company has achieved TRL 7-8 with real-world pilots in social housing via the Ofgem-funded SHIELD project, and is scaling toward 2,000 units/year production.
executive_summary.strongest_themes: Residential decarbonisation, waste heat recovery, gas boiler replacement, and fuel poverty alleviation are the strongest funding themes — directly aligned with UK government net zero priorities and Welsh Government innovation support. The dual benefit of decarbonising both heating and cloud infrastructure is a compelling differentiator for climate-focused funders.
executive_summary.strongest_geographies: Wales and the broader UK are the strongest funding geographies. Welsh Government support is already established, and UK national programmes (Ofgem SIF, SHDF, Innovate UK) are directly relevant. EU programmes are accessible via Horizon association but require consortium-building effort.
executive_summary.key_constraints: Thermify's most relevant UK programmes (Ofgem SIF, SHDF) require a licensed or registered entity as lead applicant, meaning Thermify must participate as a technology partner rather than lead — dependent on identifying and securing suitable lead partners. The EIC Accelerator is highly competitive with a complex multi-stage process. No confirmed open windows exist for several otherwise strong programmes.

strategic_recommendations.best_fit_strategy: Pursue Welsh Government SMART FIS immediately as the highest-confidence direct grant. Simultaneously build the EIC Accelerator application as a high-value Big Bet. Cultivate relationships with registered social landlords and DNOs to unlock SHDF and SIF Cycle 6 partner routes, leveraging the existing SHIELD consortium relationships.
strategic_recommendations.best_geographies: Wales (SMART FIS, Welsh Government ecosystem) and the broader UK (Ofgem SIF, SHDF, Innovate UK) are the top priorities. EU programmes are a medium-term opportunity once Horizon consortium partners are identified.
strategic_recommendations.strongest_pathways: 1) Welsh Government SMART FIS — direct application, open now, strong existing relationship; 2) EIC Accelerator — transformational funding potential, apply to next 2026 cut-off; 3) Ofgem SIF Cycle 6 — partner route via existing SHIELD consortium (UK Power Networks or Eastlight as lead); 4) SHDF Wave 3/successor — partner route via Eastlight Community Homes or similar RSL.
strategic_recommendations.key_partnerships: UK Power Networks and Eastlight Community Homes (existing SHIELD partners) are the most immediately valuable — they can serve as lead applicants for SIF Cycle 6 and SHDF respectively. Identifying a Welsh RSL or local authority partner would unlock additional social housing decarbonisation funding. An EU university or research institute partner would unlock Horizon Europe CL5.
strategic_recommendations.capability_gaps: Thermify needs to demonstrate commercial scalability (2,000+ units/year) and robust data security/privacy credentials for cloud compute workloads processed in homes — both are likely scrutinised in grant assessments. A clear cost-per-tonne-of-CO2-abated metric would strengthen applications across all programmes.
strategic_recommendations.key_risks: Dependency on partner-led routes for the largest UK programmes (SIF, SHDF) means funding is contingent on third-party willingness to lead applications. EIC Accelerator has a very low success rate (~5-10%). Smart Grants pause and NZIP conclusion reduce the direct UK grant landscape. UK Horizon association status, while confirmed, adds administrative complexity for EU programmes.

company_profile.name: Thermify
company_profile.value_proposition: Thermify replaces domestic gas boilers with distributed micro data centre units (HeatHubs) that capture waste heat from cloud computing to warm homes and heat hot water, simultaneously decarbonising residential heating and cloud infrastructure.
company_profile.technology: Distributed micro data centre nodes (HeatHub) installed in homes and garden sheds that process encrypted cloud compute workloads; waste heat generated by the compute process is captured and transferred directly into the home's central heating and hot water system, eliminating the need for separate cooling infrastructure and replacing gas boilers.
company_profile.primary_outcome: Reduction in residential carbon emissions by eliminating gas boiler dependency, while also reducing data centre cooling energy consumption.
secondary_benefits: Lower or zero-cost heating for low-income and vulnerable households
New revenue stream for homeowners hosting HeatHub units
Reduced data centre cooling energy and associated emissions
Support for social housing decarbonisation programmes
company_profile.trl: TRL 7-8 — HeatHub units have been piloted in real homes including social housing via the Ofgem-funded SHIELD project with UK Power Networks, Eastlight Community Homes, and other partners; a garden shed deployment was publicly documented in late 2025; production scale-up to 2,000 units/year is underway.
company_profile.website_summary: Thermify develops the HeatHub, a small distributed data centre unit installed in domestic homes that processes cloud computing workloads and captures the resulting waste heat to replace a gas boiler for space heating and hot water. Businesses pay to use the distributed compute network (Thermify Cloud), while homeowners receive low or no-cost heat in return. The model simultaneously decarbonises residential heating and cloud infrastructure, with a particular focus on benefits for low-income and vulnerable households.
company_profile.external_findings: Thermify has secured real-world validation through the Ofgem Strategic Investment-funded SHIELD project (2023), a consortium including UK Power Networks, Eastlight Community Homes, Essex County Council, and Citizens Advice Essex, which piloted HeatHub units in social housing. The Welsh Government has actively supported Thermify's relocation to Wales, with ambitions to scale to 40,000 HeatHub units per year within 3–5 years. The company has run at least one EIS-eligible crowdfunding campaign on Seedrs/Republic, attracting over 255 investors, with funds earmarked for production scale-up toward 2,000 units per year and development of a next-generation HeatHub V2.
